en: 5. The Chapter on Truths (Saccayamaka) 5.2 The Section on Occurrence (Pavattivāra) 5.2.3 The Subsection on Arising and Cessation (Uppādanirodhavāra)
5.2.3.1 Present Section (Paccuppannavāra) 5.2.3.1.1 Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) arises,
for that person does origination-truth (samudayasacca) cease? No.
Or, for whom the truth of the origin ceases, does the truth of suffering arise for that person? No.
For whom the truth of suffering arises, does the truth of the path cease for that person? No.
Or, for whom the truth of the path ceases, does the truth of suffering arise for that person? No.
Does the truth of the origin arise for that person for whom the truth of the path ceases? No.
Or rather, does the truth of the origin arise for that person for whom the truth of the path ceases? No.
5.2.3.1.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa).
Where the truth of suffering arises, does the truth of origination cease there?
In the case of non-percipient beings, the truth of suffering arises there, but the truth of origination does not cease there… [as before].
(The "Where" section is the same in the arising section, the cessation section, and the arising-and-cessation section; there is no difference.)

5.2.3.1.3. Positive Person-Space (Anuloma-puggalokāsa) In whom, and in what [plane], does the truth of suffering arise, while for that same person, in that same [plane], the truth of origin ceases? No.
(The "in whom" [yassa] and "in whom and in what" [yassayattha] sections are identical.)
5.2.3.1.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) does not arise, for them origination-truth (samudayasacca) does not cease?
At the moment of the dissolution of craving (taṇhā), for those persons suffering-truth does not arise; yet it is not the case that origination-truth does not [cease] for them.

It ceases. For all those passing away, for one during the course of existence at the moment of the dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from craving, and for those at the moment of the arising of the Path or the Fruit in the formless realm, the truth of suffering does not arise and the truth of origin does not cease.
Or rather, for whom the truth of origin does not cease, does the truth of suffering not arise for them?
For all those being reborn and for those during the course of existence at the moment of the arising of consciousness, the truth of the origin does not cease;

yet it is not the case that the truth of suffering does not arise for them. For all those passing away, for those during the course of existence at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness dissociated from craving, and for those in the formless realm at the moment of the arising of the path or the fruit, the truth of the origin does not [cease].
Does the truth of suffering cease and the truth of the path not arise?
For whom the truth of suffering does not arise, does the truth of the path not cease for them?
At the moment of the cessation of the path, for those [beings], the truth of suffering does not arise, yet it is not the case that the truth of the path does not cease for them.
For all those passing away, at the moment of the dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from the path during the course of existence,
and for those in the immaterial plane at the moment of the arising of the path and its fruit, the truth of suffering does not arise and the truth of the path does not cease.
Or rather, for whomsoever the truth of the path does not cease, does the truth of suffering not arise for them?
For all those being reborn and for those during the arising phase of consciousness in the course of existence, the truth of the path does not cease;

yet it is not the case that the truth of suffering does not arise for them. For all those passing away, for those during the dissolution phase of consciousness dissociated from the path in the course of existence, and for those in the formless realm at the moment of the arising of either the path or its fruition, neither the truth of the path nor [the truth of suffering] ceases.
And the truth of suffering does not arise.
For whom the truth of origination does not arise, does the truth of the path not cease for them?
At the moment of the dissolution of the path, for those [beings], the truth of origination does not arise; yet it is not the case that the truth of the path does not cease for them.

It ceases. At the moment of arising of a consciousness dissociated from craving, at the moment of dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from the Path, and for those who have attained cessation or for non-percipient beings, neither the truth of origin nor the truth of the path arises, nor does the truth of the path cease.
Or rather: for whom the truth of the path does not cease, for that person does the truth of origin not arise?
At the moment of arising of craving, the truth of the path does not cease for those persons, yet the truth of the origin does not fail to arise for them.
At the moment of dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from the path, at the moment of arising of a consciousness dissociated from craving,
for those who have attained cessation, and for non-percipient beings, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of the origin ceases or arises.
5.2.3.1.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa):
Where the truth of suffering does not arise … [etc. … 5.2.3.1.6.
Negative Person-Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa)
For whom, where, the truth of suffering does not arise …pe….
(The sections "for whom" and "for whom, where" are identical; however, in the "for whom, where" section, the phrase "those who have attained cessation" should not be included.
5.2.3.2. Past Section.
5.2.3.2.1. Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) had arisen, for that person did origination-truth (samudayasacca) cease? Yes. Or conversely...? Yes.
(Just as the past questions were analyzed in the section on arising, so too in the section on arising and cessation should they be analyzed both in direct and reverse order.
5.2.3.3. Future Section 5.2.3.3.1.
Direct Person (Anulomapuggala)
For whom suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) will arise, for them origination-truth (samudayasacca) will cease?

For those possessing the supreme path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately following [this moment] will attain the supreme path—for these, suffering-truth will arise, but for them origination-truth will not cease. For others...
For them, both the truth of suffering will arise and the truth of the origin will cease.
Or, for whomsoever ... [etc.]? Yes.
For whomsoever the truth of suffering will arise, for him the truth of the path will cease?
At the moment of the cessation of the supreme path (aggamagga), for Arahants and for those worldlings (puthujjana) who will not attain the path,
the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) will arise, but the truth of the path (maggasacca) will not cease for them.
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path, for one whose consciousness immediately precedes the attainment of the supreme path, and for others who will attain the path...
For those persons, both the truth of suffering will arise and the truth of the path will cease.
Or, for whomsoever... [etc.]? Yes.
For whomsoever the truth of the origin will arise, will the truth of the path cease for that person? Yes.
For those ordinary persons who will not attain the path, the truth of the origin will arise,
but the truth of the path will not cease for them. For those who will attain the path,
both the truth of the origin will arise and the truth of the path will cease.
Or, for whom the truth of the path will cease, will the truth of the origin arise for them?

At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), and for those who will attain the supreme path immediately after that thought-moment, the truth of the path will cease, but the truth of the origin will not arise for them. [This applies to] those who will attain the path.
For them, the truth of the path will cease and the truth of the origin will arise.
5.2.3.3.2. Positive Plane: Wherever the truth of suffering will arise …pe….
5.2.3.3.3. Positive Person-Space (Anuloma-Puggalokāsa) For whom, where suffering-truth (dukkha-sacca) will arise, for that person there, origination-truth (samudaya-sacca) will cease? [It will not.
For those possessing the supreme path (aggamagga), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the supreme path.
For non-percipient beings, for them there [is no contact]... [and so on] ...for others, those with four aggregates and those with five aggregates, for them there [is no contact]...
[and so on]. (The "yassa" and "yassattha" formulas are identical. 5.2.3.3.4.
Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala)
For whom suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) will not arise, for that person will origination-truth (samudayasacca) not cease? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom origination-truth will not cease, for that person will suffering-truth not arise?
[It will not arise] for those possessing the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the highest path.

For them, the truth of the origin will not cease, but it is not the case that for them the truth of suffering will not arise. For those possessing the final consciousness, neither the truth of the origin nor the truth of suffering will arise.
For whomsoever the truth of suffering will not arise, will the truth of the path not cease for them? Yes.
Or rather, for whom path-truth will not cease, will suffering-truth not arise for them?

At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path (agga-magga), for Arahants, and for those worldlings who will not attain the path, path-truth will not cease, yet suffering-truth will not fail to arise for them. [This is so] for those possessing their final consciousness.
For them, neither the truth of the path will cease nor will the truth of suffering arise.
Will the truth of the path not cease for one in whom the truth of the origin will not arise?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (agga-magga), and for those who will attain the supreme path immediately after that consciousness—[for them, it will not].
The truth of origination will not arise, but it is not the case that for them the truth of the path will not cease.
At the moment of the destruction of the supreme path (agga-magga) and for Arahants, neither will the truth of origination arise nor will the truth of the path cease.
Or rather: for whomsoever the truth of the path will not cease, will the truth of origination not arise for him?
For those ordinary persons who will not attain the path, the truth of the path will not cease, yet the truth of the origin will not fail to arise for them.
At the moment of the destruction of the supreme path, for Arahants, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of the origin will cease or arise.
5.2.3.3.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa):
Where the truth of suffering will not arise … [etc. … 5.2.3.3.6.
Negative Person-Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa)
For whom and where the truth of suffering will not arise … [as before] … (The *yassaka* and *yassayatthaka* are identical; the difference lies in the truth of origination and the truth of the path.
At the moment of the cessation of the final path, and for Arahants and non-percipient beings, for them there, the truth of the path will also not cease.)
And the truth of origination will not arise.
5.2.3.4. Chapter on the Present and the Past (Paccuppannātītavāra) 5.2.3.4.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala)
For whom the truth of suffering arises, for that person did the truth of the origin cease? Yes.

Or conversely... [as before]. (The questions concerning the present and the past—whether in the section on arising, the section on arising and ceasing, those concerning "for whom," those concerning "where," those concerning "for whom and where," and both the direct and inverse orders—are all similar; they should be analyzed without confusion.)
5.2.3.5. Chapter on the Present and Future (Paccuppannānāgatavāra) 5.2.3.5.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) arises, for that person will origination-truth (samudayasacca) cease?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), at the moment of the arising of the consciousness of Arahants,
and at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path— suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) arises for them,
but origination-truth (samudayasacca) will not cease for them. For others who are being reborn, and during the course of existence (pavatta) for [those with] consciousness...
At the moment of arising, both the truth of suffering and the truth of origination arise for them, and the truth of origination will cease.
Or rather, for whomsoever the truth of origination will cease, does the truth of suffering arise for that person?
For all those passing away, at the moment of the cessation of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the moment of the arising of the Path and the Fruit in the formless realm.
For them, the truth of the origin will cease, but the truth of suffering does not arise for them.
For all those being reborn, and during the phase of the arising of consciousness in the course of existence, both the truth of the origin will cease and the truth of suffering arises for them.
For whom suffering-truth arises, for that person will path-truth cease?

For Arahants at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and for those worldlings who will not attain the path at the moment of rebirth-linking and during the course of existence at the moment of the arising of consciousness— for them, suffering-truth arises, but [path-truth does not cease].

For them, the truth of the path will cease. At the moment of arising of the supreme path; at the moment of arising of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path; for others who will attain the path;
and for those being reborn during the moment of arising of the consciousness in the course of existence—for these, the truth of suffering arises.
And the truth of the path will cease.
Or else, for whomsoever the truth of the path will cease, does the truth of suffering arise for them?
For that person who will attain the supreme path immediately after a certain state of consciousness, at the moment of the dissolution of that consciousness—those...
For others who will attain the path, at the moment of their death, at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness during the course of existence (*pavatta*),

and at the moment of the arising of the path and its fruition in the formless realm (*arūpa*), the truth of the path (*maggasacca*) will cease for them, but the truth of suffering (*dukkhasacca*) does not arise for them.
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (*aggamagga*), [this occurs] for that consciousness immediately preceding the supreme path...

At the moment of the arising of that consciousness, and for others who will attain the path at the moment of rebirth or during the course of existence at the moment of the arising of consciousness— their truth of the path will cease and the truth of suffering will arise.
For one in whom the truth of the origin arises, will the truth of the path cease?
For those ordinary persons who will not attain the path, at the moment craving arises in them, the truth of the origin arises,
but the truth of the path will not cease for them. For those who will attain the path,
at the moment craving arises in them, both the truth of the origin arises and the truth of the path will cease.
Or, for whom the truth of the path will cease, does the truth of the origin arise for them?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path; at the moment of the dissolution of craving in those whose consciousness immediately following that [moment] will attain the supreme path;
and in those others who will attain the path, while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring.
For those who have attained the attainment of cessation and for non-percipient beings, the truth of the path will cease,
but the truth of the origin does not arise for them. For those who will attain the path at the moment craving arises,
both the truth of the path will cease and the truth of the origin will arise.
5.2.3.5.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa):
Where the truth of suffering arises … [as above] … 5.2.3.5.3.
Positive Person-Plane (Anuloma-puggalokāsa)
For whom, and where, does the truth of suffering arise, and for that same person, will the truth of the origin cease there?
[It will] for one at the moment of the arising of the supreme path; for Arahants at the moment of the arising of consciousness;

for one whose consciousness immediately precedes the attainment of the supreme path, at the moment of the arising of that consciousness; and for those being reborn in the realm of non-percipient beings.

For those [beings] there, the truth of suffering [arises] …pe… for others who are being reborn in the fourfold or fivefold plane, and during the phase of the arising of consciousness in the course of existence, for them there the truth of suffering [arises] …pe…. Or,
for whomsoever the truth of the origin will cease at a certain place, does the truth of suffering arise for that person at that place?

For those passing away from the four-aggregate or five-aggregate planes, at the moment of the cessation of consciousness during the course of existence, and for those in the formless plane at the moment of the arising of the Path or the Fruit—cessation-truth (samudaya-sacca) will cease there for them, but suffering-truth (dukkha-sacca) does not arise there for them.
For those being reborn into the four-aggregate or five-aggregate planes, during the course of existence... [of consciousness]...
At the moment of arising, origination-truth will cease and suffering-truth arises for those [beings] there.
For whomsoever suffering-truth arises there, will path-truth cease there for them?
[It will not cease] for Arahants at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those bound for the states of misery, and for those worldlings who will not attain the path.

For those beings at the moment of rebirth, for those during the arising phase of a consciousness in the course of existence, and for those at the moment of rebirth in the realm of non-percipient beings, the truth of suffering arises there;

yet the truth of the path will not cease for them there. At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (agga-magga), and at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately preceding one who will attain the supreme path, [the truth of suffering arises, but the truth of the path will not cease].
For those others who will attain the path, at the moment of their rebirth and during the arising phase of consciousness in the course of existence,
both the truth of suffering arises and the truth of the path will cease there.
Or rather, for whomsoever the truth of the path will cease in a certain place, does the truth of suffering arise for them in that same place?
In one whose consciousness immediately precedes the attainment of the supreme path—at the moment of the dissolution of that consciousness;
in others who will attain the path at the moment of death; in those during the course of existence at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness;
and in those in the formless realm at the moment of the arising of the path and its fruit—the truth of the path will cease there, but [the truth of suffering will not].
For them, the truth of suffering arises therein. At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga),
at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path, for those others who will attain the path,
and for those being reborn during the course of existence (pavatta) at the moment of the arising of consciousness— for all these, the truth of the path will cease therein.
And the truth of suffering arises.
For whom and where the truth of the origin arises, for that person and in that place, will the truth of the path cease? [It will not.
For those bound for the states of deprivation and for those worldlings who will not attain the path at the moment of the arising of craving.
For them, the truth of origination arises there, but the truth of the path will not cease for them there.
For those who will attain the path at the moment of the arising of craving, both the truth of origination arises and the truth of the path will cease for them there.
Or rather, for whomsoever the truth of the path will cease at a certain place, does the truth of the origin arise for that person at that place?

[Answer: At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga); at the moment of the dissolution of craving for those whose consciousness immediately following this will attain the supreme path; and for others who will attain the path, while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring.
For them, the truth of the path will cease there, but the truth of the origin does not arise for them there.
For those who will attain the path at the moment of the arising of craving, for them both the truth of the path will cease and the truth of the origin will arise there.
5.2.3.5.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom suffering-truth (dukkha-sacca) does not arise, for that person will origination-truth (samudaya-sacca) not cease?
For all those passing away, during the moment of the cessation of consciousness in the course of existence, and at the moment of the arising of the Path and the Fruit in the formless realm.
For them, the truth of suffering does not arise, yet it is not the case that for them the truth of the origin will not cease.

This is at the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path; at the moment of the dissolution of the consciousness of Arahants; at the moment of the dissolution of that consciousness immediately after which one will attain the supreme path;
and at the moment of the arising of both the supreme path and its fruit in the formless realm.
For them, neither the truth of suffering arises nor will the truth of origination cease.
Or rather: for whom the truth of origination will not cease, does the truth of suffering not arise for that person?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path, at the moment of the arising of the consciousness of Arahants, and for that consciousness immediately after which...
At the moment of the arising of that consciousness for those who will attain the supreme path, the truth of origination will not cease,
yet the truth of suffering does not fail to arise for them. At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path, at the moment of the dissolution of the consciousness of Arahants,
and at the moment of the dissolution of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path—
In the formless realm, and at the moment of the arising of the highest path and its fruit,
origination-truth will not cease and suffering-truth does not arise for them.
For whom suffering-truth does not arise, will path-truth not cease for them?
At the moment of dissolution of that consciousness after which they will attain the supreme path;
at the moment of death of those others who will attain the path; at the moment of dissolution of the consciousness during the course of existence;
and at the moment of the arising of both the path and its fruit in the formless realm—for these, the truth of suffering does not arise, but the truth of the path does not fail to arise for them.
It will not cease. At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path, at the moment of the dissolution of the consciousness of Arahants,
at the moment of death of those worldlings who will not attain the path, during the course of existence at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness,
and at the moment of the arising of the fruit of Arahantship in the formless realm— for these, the truth of suffering does not arise and the truth of the path will not cease.
Or again, for whom path-truth will not cease, does suffering-truth not arise?

For Arahants at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and for those worldlings who will not attain the path at the moment of rebirth-linking or during the course of existence at the moment of the arising of consciousness— for them, path-truth will not cease.
And yet, the truth of suffering does not fail to arise for them. At the moment of the cessation of the supreme path, at the moment of the cessation of the consciousness of Arahants,
for those worldlings who will not attain the path at the time of their death, at the moment of the cessation of consciousness during the course of existence,
and at the moment of the arising of the fruit of Arhatship in the formless realm— for these, the truth of the path will not cease.
And the truth of suffering does not arise.
For whom the truth of the origin does not arise, will the truth of the path not cease for them?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), for one who will attain the supreme path immediately after that consciousness, and for others...

For those who will attain the path at the moment of the dissolution of craving, while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, for those who have attained cessation (nirodhasamāpanna), and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), the truth of the origin (samudayasacca) does not arise; yet it is not the case that the truth of the path (maggasacca) will not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path (aggamagga), for Arahants and for those worldlings (puthujjana) who do not [attain the path]...
Will origination-truth not arise and path-truth not cease for those [persons] at the moment of the destruction of craving, while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring?
Or rather, for whom path-truth will not cease, for that person does origination-truth not arise?
For those ordinary persons who will not attain the path, at the moment of the arising of their craving, the truth of the path will not cease;

yet it is not that the truth of the origin does not arise for them. At the moment of the dissolution of the craving of those ordinary persons who will not attain the path—at the moment of the dissolution of craving for those ordinary persons who will not attain the path, and at the moment of the dissolution of the final path for Arahants—[the truth of the path will not cease].
When a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, for those [beings], the truth of the path will not cease and the truth of the origin will not arise.
5.2.3.5.5. Negative Spatial Analysis:
Where the truth of suffering does not arise …pe….
5.2.3.5.6. Negative Person-Space (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa) For whom, where suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) does not arise, for that person there, will origination-truth (samudayasacca) not cease?

[It will not cease] for those passing away from the four-aggregate or five-aggregate planes, during the dissolution-moment of consciousness in the course of existence, and for those on the path in the immaterial plane.
At the moment of the arising of the fruit, suffering-truth does not arise for those persons there,
yet origination-truth will not cease for them there. At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path, at the moment of the dissolution of the consciousness of Arahants,
at the moment of the dissolution of that consciousness immediately after which one will attain the supreme path, and in the formless realm—

At the moment of the arising of the highest path and its fruit, and for those passing away from the realm of non-percipient beings, neither the truth of suffering nor the truth of origination arises there. Or conversely:
for whomsoever the truth of origination will not cease there, does the truth of suffering not arise for them there?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), at the moment of the arising of the consciousness of Arahants,
at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path, and for those reborn in the sphere of non-percipient beings (asaññasatta)—
for these, origination-truth (samudayasacca) will not cease there, yet suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) does not fail to arise there for them.
At the moment of the destruction of the supreme path (aggamagga), at the moment of the destruction of the consciousness of Arahants,
at the moment of the destruction of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path, at the moment of the arising of the supreme path and its fruit in the formless realm,
and for those passing away from the non-percipient beings— among these, the truth of origination (samudayasacca) does not cease there.
And the truth of suffering does not arise.
For whom and where the truth of suffering does not arise, for that person and in that place, will the truth of the path not cease?
For those who will attain the supreme path immediately after a particular moment of consciousness—at the moment of the dissolution of that consciousness—[for them...]

For others who will attain the path, at the moment of the cessation of consciousness during their life-process as they pass away, and at the moment of the arising of the path and the fruit in the formless realm, suffering-truth does not arise for them there;
yet it is not the case that path-truth will not cease for them there. [This is so] at the moment of the cessation of the highest path for Arahants.
At the moment of the cessation of consciousness in those destined for states of misery, in worldlings who will not attain the path at the time of their death,

during the course of existence at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, at the moment of the arising of the highest fruit (arahantship) in the formless realm, and in those non-percipient beings at the moment of their death—
therein the truth of suffering does not arise and the truth of the path will not cease.
Or conversely: for whom, wherever the truth of the path will not cease, does the truth of suffering not arise there?

[It does not arise] for Arahants at the moment of the arising of consciousness; for those bound for the states of misery; for those ordinary persons who will not attain the path at the moment of rebirth;
during the course of existence, for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness; and for those at the moment of rebirth among non-percipient beings.
In that case, the truth of the path will not cease, yet the truth of suffering does not fail to arise for them there.

This is at the moment of the cessation of the supreme path (agga-magga), at the moment of the cessation of the consciousness of Arahants, for those bound for the states of misery (āpāyika), for those worldlings (puthujjana) who will not attain the path at the moment of their death,
and during the course of existence (pavatta) at the moment of the cessation of consciousness for those in the formless realm (arūpa) attaining the fruit of the supreme path.
At the moment of arising for those non-percipient beings who are passing away, the truth of the path will not cease there, and the truth of suffering does not arise.
For whom, where the truth of the origin does not arise, will the truth of the path not cease there?
At the moment of arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), for one whose consciousness immediately precedes the attainment of the supreme path, and for others...
For those who will attain the path, at the moment of the dissolution of craving while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, origination-truth does not arise therein;
yet it is not the case that path-truth will not cease therein for them.
[This is true] at the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path, for Arahants, for those bound for the states of misery, and for those worldlings who will not attain the path.

In those persons, at the moment of the dissolution of craving, while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, and in the case of non-percipient beings—therein, neither the truth of origination arises nor will the truth of the path cease. Or conversely:
for whomsoever, wherever the truth of the path will not cease, does the truth of origination not arise therein for them?
For those bound for the states of misery and for those worldlings who will not attain the path—at the moment craving arises in them—the truth of the path will not cease there;
yet it is not the case that the truth of the origin does not arise for them there.
[This is also the case] at the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path, for Arahants, for those bound for the states of misery, and for those worldlings who will not attain the path.

For those at the moment of the dissolution of craving, while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, and for non-percipient beings, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of the origin will cease there, nor does the truth of the origin arise. 5.2.3.6.
Chapter on the Past and Future.
5.2.3.6.1. Positive Person (Anuloma-puggala) For whom suffering-truth (dukkha-sacca) has arisen, will origination-truth (samudaya-sacca) cease for that person?

(Just as in the section on cessation (nirodha-vāra), the questions concerning the past and future were analyzed both positively and negatively, so too in this section on arising and cessation, they should be analyzed without confusion.)
The Section on Arising and Cessation.
